Every figure and prop is a few flat cut-paper shapes. Every figure and prop has a thick warm dark-brown ink outline and a thin light inner edge just inside it, and is creased once by a single straight diagonal line at the light's angle, its far side a deeper hue of its own colour turned toward violet, never grey and never black. A head is ONE simple shape inside one single thick outline, and the light inner edge runs round that one outline. Garments are flat planes: no pockets, no buttons, no stitching, no seams, no cuffs, no fabric texture. Hands are plain round paper circles at the end of each arm in its sleeve, the sleeve running from the shoulder to the hand: never a hand floating free of the body, never a bare arm, no thumbs, no fingers. Faces are three marks only: two small dark ink oval eyes, short brows and a one-line mouth. One muted hue per piece. The light: a warm, soft key light from the upper left; a soft paper grain on every piece and every plane; a small soft violet contact shadow under each figure, never a darker brown; a muted, warm palette in which only the film's accents are loud. Keep it K1: no white sticker border round the figures, no felt or stitching style, no big glossy eyes, no realistic anatomy. The look is stylised, attractive, expressive and minimal.

Loose, wavy, mid-brown hair over the tops of his ears and down beside them to the jaw, curling at its ends, its shade a deeper brown; warm light-tan skin; small dark oval eyes, short dark brows and a one-line mouth. His chin meets his neck by a shade step, a darker band of skin at the top of the neck, never an ink line across the chin. A plain long-sleeved round-neck top in a muted teal, hanging just past his waist to a straight hem; khaki trousers with a narrow brown band at the waist under the top's hem; plain dark-brown shoes. Each sleeve is the top's own teal paper, a soft tube from the shoulder to the wrist that ends in a plain straight open edge round the hand, and each hand is a plain round circle of his skin at its sleeve's end. Wherever a sleeve lies in front of his body, the sleeve is its own piece of paper laid over the top: the thick warm ink outline runs along its whole length where it lies over the top, as his kept pose sheet outlines the forearms held in front of him, its lit upper edge a step lighter teal and its underside, where it lies against the top, a deeper teal turned toward violet, so the arm never melts into the top's colour. His head is one simple shape.
